description: A *landmark* is a fact that is true at some point of every plan. This method finds fact landmarks in the delete relaxation, where facts stay true once reached. Each fact gets a label: the facts that every relaxed path to it makes true no later than the fact itself. A fact of the state has itself as label; an operator offers its effect the union of its preconditions' labels plus the effect; a fact keeps the intersection of all its offers. The landmarks are the goal facts and their labels, and each fact in a label is *naturally ordered* before that landmark. The result is sound for the real task and feeds landmark heuristics such as the landmark count and landmark cost partitioning.

papers.title: Landmark Extraction via Planning Graph Propagation

papers.authors: Emil Keyder, Silvia Richter, Malte Helmert
papers.title: Sound and Complete Landmarks for And/Or Graphs
